goal: Maximize believable live-action Satoshi performance while minimizing visible generative artifacts.

defaults.pose: seated, leaning, or lightly occupied; avoid rigid standing presenter pose
defaults.hands: visible when practical, naturally resting or making small gestures
defaults.camera: stable, eye-level or slightly off-axis; avoid dramatic low angles
defaults.movement: small head turns, blinks, breath, restrained hand motion
defaults.character_input: image for conversational scenes; video only when inherited scene/camera motion is editorially necessary

rules: Prefer waist-up framing; never make the head dominate the body.
Avoid full-body talking shots unless the action is essential.
Prefer seated or task-oriented staging to standing still and addressing camera.
Use image-based Act Two for short conversational beats when body/camera motion need not be inherited.
Use character-video Act Two only when the source video's body/environment motion is specifically desirable.
Keep visible speaking takes short and cut away before synthetic motion becomes repetitive.
Expression intensity defaults to 2; raise only when a reviewed test justifies it.
Match the driving performance pose to the character image pose as closely as possible.
Place Satoshi slightly off-center when the environment/prop is editorially meaningful.
A speaking shot should contain one physical task or relationship to the environment when possible: seated at cabinet, holding folder, looking at monitor, turning from evidence to camera.
Do not ask Satoshi to simply stand in an empty scene and deliver exposition.
editing_tricks: enter the speaking shot after motion has already begun
cut away on noun or punchline rather than waiting for a static pause
use J-cuts/L-cuts so voice can start before or continue after the face is visible
return to Satoshi only for persona-bearing words
use 2-5 second host shots inside longer narration
avoid holding on the final generated frame
